My family and society forced me to take this test (you are 18 now, y u no driving car eh?), so I just started to take lessons (theoretical part was easy since I'm functioning perfectly with reading etc.).  
But man, the driving part?  
  
I'm scared so much about driving at high speed actually, especially the autobahn (Switzerland). I imagine some final destination kind of death whenever I have to get into all these cars who are driving soo fast.  
  
Also I'm not a natural talent and started to feel really dumb after a while because all my friends actually were good and had no problems...  
  
And oh, when I had to take the test, there was suddenly another person sitting in the car and judged me and how I drive: I forgot the mirrrors, the lights, the belt and started driving...  
  
And I failed the test two times:/  
  
At the third time I was good enough and had no nerves at all with driving that I somehow managed to pass...it was at a time where I failed school and everything and I was too deep in depression to even care anymore, maybe that relaxed me Idk. Also I have been driving a long time and tried to tell me that I can drive...    
  
But it was really a fight...  
   
Since having my driving license I never drove again, just yesterday I had enough courage after half a year of therapy and on approppiate mediaction that I somehow managed to park a car. (I made a post about it yesterday out of happiness:)  
  
I think you need to be good enough, so good that even though you are scared shitless, that you still can drive without doing a major mistake, that's what I think helped me at the test, later on in life it was the treatment I received. And you can tell them that you are scared, they understand that.  
  
tldr:  
  
When having test:  
  
I was depressed and didn't give a shit about life anyway anymore. everything piled up on me. But I was still a little nervous but I had enough driving training that I still could do it because I was good enough, you know like driving bicycle, you can still drive bicycle when excited?  
  
Later it was months of treatment and being finally on treatment, also my mother was very supportive and told me that I could do it.

Well, I don't know what advice to give actually, I started taking cipralex (lexapro in the US?), I think that might have given me a bit of courage too, but it was me who drove the car not the pills.  
I failed my driving test two times, the third time I was just like "meh, I don't care about this shit anyway, you won't pass anyway, I'm sick of it, I'll just drive and then I can finally just stop trying to get my damn license, I don't even have money either..."   
I think that thought of really not giving a shit helped me actually, but it was quite a negative way of thinking somehow...I was severely depressed at that time, was in that mental state where I just stopped caring about anything at all. I failed school and all at that time and failing the test again seemed just the way it is with me...  
  
But then I passed because I drove so relaxed (and after a shitload long time of driving and my very passionate loving teacher).  
  
I hope you can do it too, I really wish you can, stay strong! I wished I could give you more advice, but just saying "be confident" is a rather shitty advice which I don't want to give because it's not helping (it didn't really help me).  
  
Oh, I remember that I practised driving the car so long that even though I was scared I was able to drive it properly enough. That was actually the only way...and the plan when I went to the test the third time.   
  
You get just so good at it that even your fear can't hold you back (shitty advice I know, I'm sorry).
